findings.reasoning: When header is genuinely not the start of fullHeader, _fastaDefline writes "name + space + long name" (12455), so the defline begins with the short name. Read-back strips exactly one '>' (8734) and takes the first word (8735) as header, with the whole cleaned line stored as fullHeader (8739): the name comes back first and the long name survives intact. The one gap: if the short name itself contains a space, 8735 keeps only its first word - which is exactly finding 1, since Rename (14494/14495) is the only setter that can put a spaced name in .header; every other setter derives header from the first word of fullHeader (27779, 27844).
findings.scenario: A NEXUS-style row (header "Homo_sapiens", fullHeader "Homo sapiens") is written as ">Homo_sapiens Homo sapiens" and reads back as header "Homo_sapiens" with long name "Homo sapiens" preserved.
findings.title: The 12455 branch (name first, then long name) round-trips correctly because the parser names rows by the defline's first word

It then sets BOTH fields: 14494 `state.seqs[index].header = newName;` and 14495 `state.seqs[index].fullHeader = newName;`. So a spaced name makes full === header === "mus mus"; _fastaDefline (12452-12456) line 12454 `if (!full || !q.header || full.startsWith(q.header)) return full;` returns "mus mus" and the file gets ">mus mus". On read-back, parseFasta keeps the whole defline (8863 `header = isPir ? '>' + line.slice(4) : line;`) and _pushParsedFastaSequence keeps only the first word: 8735 `const displayHeader = cleanHeader.split(/\s+/)[0] || 'unnamed';`. The Sequence editor deliberately avoids this by deriving the short name from the first word (27844 `const newHeader = newFullHeader.split(/\s+/)[0];`, 27779 `state.seqs[idx].header = fullH.split(/\s+/)[0];`); Rename is the one path that does not.
findings.scenario: Double-click a row name, type "mus mus", press Enter, then Save (or Copy) and reopen the file: the defline is ">mus mus" and the row comes back named "mus". Any name colour assigned to "mus mus" also fails to match after reload.
findings.title: Rename accepts a name with a space, but the defline read back keeps only the first word, so the saved/loaded row gets a different name

findings.reasoning: Case (a). The hypothesised state (header "seq1", fullHeader "seq10 Homo") cannot be produced: Rename sets both fields to the same string (14494, 14495 `state.seqs[index].fullHeader = newName;`), and the Sequence editor always derives the short name from the first word of the long name (27844, 27779), so full.startsWith(header) is trivially true with full === header === "seq1". _fastaDefline returns full = "seq1"; the written defline is ">seq1" and the row reads back as "seq1" (8735). The prefix trap would only fire if some code set .header alone; today every .header setter also sets .fullHeader (14494/14495) or derives it from fullHeader's first word (27779; 27868 `state.seqs[index].header = newHeader;` with newHeader built at 27844).
findings.scenario: Rename a row whose long name was "seq10 Homo" to "seq1": full is "seq1", defline written ">seq1", name read back "seq1". No name is lost.
findings.title: (a) The prefix trap (name "seq1", long name "seq10 Homo") is unreachable from Rename, which overwrites the long name too

findings.reasoning: Case (c). Rename to ">seq" is accepted (14529 trims only; 14487 does not reject it) and sets header=fullHeader=">seq"; _fastaDefline returns the full text unchanged (12454) so the line written is ">>seq". parseFasta treats any line starting with '>' as ONE defline: 8857 `if (line.startsWith('>')) {` and 8863 `header = isPir ? '>' + line.slice(4) : line;` keep the whole line; 8734 strips exactly one leading '>' leaving ">seq", and 8735 names the row ">seq". So ViewAlign round-trips the strange name (no data loss, no extra record), at the cost of an ambiguous ">>seq" line for other tools. A '>' elsewhere in the name ("seq>1") also round-trips.

findings.title: (c) A name starting with '>' round-trips (parser strips only one '>') but exports a line ">>seq" that other tools may reject or split

findings.reasoning: Case (d). An empty name cannot be produced: the input is trimmed at 14529 and 14487 rejects the empty string. An empty fullHeader (possible only from parsing a bare ">" line) makes _fastaDefline's `!full` guard (12454) return "" (not undefined), so a bare ">" is written; on read-back header = ">" (8863), 8734 strips the '>' leaving "", and 8735's `|| 'unnamed'` names the row "unnamed" (8739 stores fullHeader: cleanHeader = ""). No row is dropped. I did not find any other route to an empty fullHeader, so the claim covers the parse-then-save cycle and Rename.
findings.scenario: Type only spaces in the rename box: nothing changes (14487 rejects). A file with a bare ">" line: row loads as "unnamed", saves as ">", reloads as "unnamed" again.
findings.title: (d) Empty names are impossible from Rename (guard at 14487) and an empty long name degrades to a bare '>' that reads back as 'unnamed', so no row is lost

Rename row 2 to row 1's name: both rows then have identical header and fullHeader; _fastaDefline writes one ">name" line per row and parseFasta pushes one record per '>' line unconditionally (8863 header = line when `line.startsWith('>')` at 8857; then _pushParsedFastaSequence pushes at 8739) with no dedup, so both rows and their sequences survive with the same name. I did NOT verify the downstream by-name lookups made by seqEditApply (27725), which the prompt says matches records to rows by name, so with duplicate names that matching is ambiguous; I only claim the save/read-back cycle is lossless.

findings.title: (e) Two rows renamed to one name both survive the round-trip as two separate records with the same name

note: Q15 part 1 answered. Summary of what is written and what name comes back, all traced in script.js: (a) Rename sets BOTH header and fullHeader to the new name (14494/14495), so a name that is a prefix of the old long name's first word simply replaces the long name; defline ">seq1" reads back "seq1" — the hypothesised header="seq1"/fullHeader="seq10 Homo" state is unreachable from Rename, and the only other .header setters (27779, 27868 via 27844) derive the header from the long name's first word, keeping startsWith true — so the 12454 branch can never silently drop a short name today. (b) DEFECT: Rename only trims (14529) and only rejects empty names (14487); "mus mus" is stored in header and fullHeader, _fastaDefline returns the untouched full text (12454), the file gets ">mus mus", and _pushParsedFastaSequence keeps only the first word (8735) — the row reloads as "mus", a different name (medium; name colours keyed by the spaced name also break). (c) ">seq" is accepted by Rename; written as ">>seq"; ViewAlign's parser treats the line as ONE defline (8857/8863) and strips exactly one '>' (8734), so the row still reads back as ">seq" — no data loss inside ViewAlign, but the exported file has an ambiguous ">>seq" line (low). (d) Empty name blocked by 14487; an empty long name yields a bare ">" that reads back as "unnamed" (8735) — no row lost. (e) Duplicate names are written as duplicate ">name" records and both rows reload unchanged (8739 pushes per '>' line with no dedup; downstream by-name lookups in the Sequence editor were not traced). The 12455 branch (name first, then long name) round-trips correctly because 8735 names rows by the defline's first word. Most serious finding: Rename's lack of the first-word normalisation that every other code path performs.
